lines: -# Runbook: Drawing set → verified Blender model + quantity takeoff
-**Owner:** Michael Colenso | **Frequency:** As needed (one run per building / drawing set)
-**Scope today:** vector-PDF plan sets (CAD-plotted). Single-story, orthogonal walls, hip/gable roofs.
-**Not yet supported:** scanned/raster drawings, photos or field measurements as geometry sources,
-multi-story, curved or skewed walls. Don't force those through this pipeline — flag them.
-Turn a drawing set into (1) a Blender model whose geometry is checked against the drawings, (2) a
-quantity takeoff workbook, and (3) review renders — every element tagged with the sheet it came
-from and whether it is **documented**, **provisional** (measured from a drawing at a verified
-scale) or **assumed**. The model is a coordination/estimating tool, not a contract document.
-Time for a first building like Cottage A: ~2–3 h of operator time; builds take ~2 min
-(review renders) or ~6 min (with realistic renders) on 2 CPU cores.
-- [ ] Python **3.11 exactly** (bpy 5.0.x wheels are cp311 only). Linux or macOS. No GPU needed.
-- [ ] The drawing set as a **vector** PDF. Test: `pdftotext -f N -l N set.pdf - | head` returns dimension
-      text such as `39-0`. If it returns nothing, the set is scanned — stop (see Escalation).
-- [ ] Sheets needed: dimensioned floor plan, roof plan, all exterior elevations, window/door schedule,
-      and the sheet that states plate/truss-bearing height (elevation or framing plan).
-Paths below are from the repo root. `PDF=sources/<project>.pdf` throughout.
-uv sync --group pdf --group vision     # downloads Python 3.11 + the locked deps into .venv
-mkdir -p sources takeoff && cp /path/to/set.pdf sources/<project>.pdf   # sources/ is git-ignored
-**If it fails:** on Linux install `libx11-6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxi6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libice6 libgl1`.
-pdftoppm -r 72 -f <page> -l <page> -png $PDF preview    # at 72 dpi, 1 pixel = 1 PDF point
-**Expected:** each page's own sheet number (title block) and drawing titles; find the floor plan, roof plan,
-elevations and schedules. A page with `-` and no titles has no text layer (raster) — those sheets can't be
-extracted. The cover/index page may show a referenced sheet number instead of its own.
-Record each sheet in the spec's `sources:` list (sheet number, title, revision/date).
-**If it fails:** no text on the plan/roof/elevation pages → scanned set → stop (Escalation).
-### Step 3 — Calibrate the plan sheet from its own dimensions
-uv run bm calibrate scale $PDF --page <plan page> --text "<overall dim, e.g. 78-0>" --feet 78
-uv run bm calibrate scale $PDF --page <plan page> --text "<another dim, e.g. 39-0>" --feet 39
-**Expected:** both give the same pt/ft (Cottage A: 18.000 = ¼"). Must agree within 0.1%.
-**If it fails:** "no bracketing ticks" → the string uses dots/arrows, try another string. Disagreement →
-one string is not-to-scale or mislabeled; use strings that agree and note it.
-### Step 4 — Find the extraction window and origin
-1. Open `preview-*.png` from Step 2 (pixels = points). Read the plan's bounding box in points → `--clip x0,y0,x1,y1`
-   (include the building, exclude title block and schedules).
-2. Centre (party wall / symmetry line) from the overall-width ticks printed in Step 3:
-3. `--rear-px` = `(rear wall face y in points − clip y0) × 24 / pt_per_ft`. Pick the rear face of the section
-(walls black, window candidates orange `W#`, door candidates blue `D#`, labelled with X,Y in inches).
-Use `--half right` only for mirror-image units (see Step 6); otherwise `--half all` is not implemented yet — escalate.
-**If it fails:** walls missing in the review image → see Troubleshooting (clouds, tags, dimension clutter).
-### Step 6 — Review the extraction (do not skip)
-- [ ] **Mirror check** (duplexes): confirm the two units are true mirrors before using `--half`. Look at the plan;
-      if in doubt, escalate — Cottage A measured 94% of walls within 1½".
-- [ ] **Every opening candidate must appear on an elevation.** For each W#/D#, find it on the matching
-      elevation; accept (copy to spec `openings:`) or reject (list in a spec comment with reason).
-      Typical false candidates: tubs/showers, garage-door lines, revision clouds, the party-wall FEC cabinet.
-- [ ] **Holes:** look for walls missing under revision clouds, tags or text. Add each as `extra_walls:` with
-1. Elevation scale: `calibrate.py scale` on an elevation string or use the sheet's stated scale (Cottage A AH500: 9 pt/ft).
-2. **Plate height** from the documented elevations (FF and truss-bearing lines) → `plate_height_in` (documented).
-3. **Window/door heads and sills**: measure on the elevation (see `src/bmodels/overlay.py` raster at 1 px/in) → provisional.
-   Nominal sizes come from the window schedule → put the mark (`mark: A`) on each opening.
-   python src/bmodels/calibrate.py outline $PDF --page <roof plan page> --clip <roof clip> --pt-per-ft <pt/ft> \
-   Take the closed loop of segments (ignore stray section-cut lines drawn at the same weight). Convert Y to the
-   plan frame (Cottage A: roof Y − 2.0 ft, because the rear eave sits 2'-0" behind the rear wall).
-5. **Roof pieces:** decompose the outline into rectangles: one `hip` per main mass, `gable` for each gable with
-   `ridge: x|y` and its gable end at the outline edge. Pitches from the roof plan (documented). Then confirm the
-   model's predicted ridge/hip positions land on the drawn ridge/hip lines (Cottage A: within 0.4').
-6. Eave height (`eave_surface_z_in`) and soffit from the elevation → provisional.
-### Step 8 — Write the spec and checks
-Create the site with `uv run bm new <site>` (once per project), copy `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-cottage-a.yaml` → `projects/<site>/specs/<project>.yaml` and fill it in. Required checks:
-- wall extents vs overall dimension strings (documented),
-- `qto_checks.plan_area_sf` if the set states a roof area anywhere (venting calcs often do).
-uv run bm build <site>/<project>              # ~2 min, review renders
-uv run bm build <site>/<project> --realistic  # ~6 min, adds hero renders
-**Expected:** `**PASS** — n/n checks`, exit code 0, and in `build/<site>/<project>/`: `.blend`, `.glb`,
-**If it fails:** the report names the failing check — fix the spec, never loosen a tolerance to pass.
-### Step 10 — Overlay the model on the elevations
-uv run bm calibrate elev $PDF --page <elev page> --clip <elevation clip> --pt-per-ft <pt/ft> \
-**Expected:** ≥ 80% edge agreement (Cottage A: front 82%, rear 87%) **and** a visual check that windows, doors,
-eaves, ridges and gables sit on the drawing's lines. The % alone is not proof.
-**If it fails:** misaligned horizontally → wrong `--center-col` (re-run `calibrate.py elev`); an element off →
-fix that element in the spec; `side` views need the building's Y-centre (not automated yet).
-- [ ] Opening counts per elevation match the drawings.
-- [ ] Any documented quantity reconciles (roof area, window count).
-- [ ] Set the **roof waste %** (yellow cell) to your standard.
-- [ ] Sanity-check gable panel sf per elevation against a hand estimate (a known past bug counted an interior plane).
-### Step 12 — Commit and let CI rebuild
-git add projects/<site> && git commit -m "Model <project>" && git push
-**Expected:** Actions run "Build & verify models" goes green; the job summary shows each `report.md`;
-**If it fails:** open the run → "Build, verify, render" step log → the failing check is printed.
-## Detail mode (sections: rake, eave, balcony edge, window head …)
-Use when the source is a **section detail**, not a plan. Spec type `detail` (example: `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-rake-ah700-12.yaml`).
-1. **Pick a true section at a stated scale.** Reject NTS / perspective sketches for geometry (AT401/4 rake is NTS — used only for sequence).
-2. **Verify the detail scale** from a dimension string inside the detail:
-   `uv run bm calibrate scale $PDF --page 8 --text "1-6" --feet 1.5` (AH700/12: 106.5 pt/ft vs 108 nominal — sheet plots 1.4% small; always use the measured value).
-3. **Section frame:** X horizontal from a named face (e.g. fascia outer face = 0), Z plumb from a named plane (e.g. underside of roof sheathing = 0). Write that in the spec header.

-4. **One component per callout**, sized by the callout's **actual** dimensions (5/4x10 = 1 × 9¼; 1x6 = ¾ × 5½), positioned from the drawing. Thicknesses stated elsewhere (wall types, structural notes) cite that sheet. Anything drawn but not called out = provisional with a `basis`; anything not drawn = assumed.

-5. **Checks:** every dimension string in the detail as a `between:` check (hard); measured drawn sizes as `drawn:` checks (warn only — they test the *drawing* against its callouts; a ⚠️ means the drawing and the callout disagree, e.g. fascia drawn 10.1" deep vs 9¼" called out).
-6. `path:` length and `pitch:` (rake follows the roof slope). `peel:` / `cutaway_step_in:` are presentation only — the near end stays a true section.
-7. Build with `--realistic` for the labeled cutaway; then

- `uv run bm detail-overlay build///.blend --pdf $PDF --page

--clip --pt-per-ft --origin-pt --out build///overlay_section.png`
-   Judge by eye: the % counts model outline beyond the detail's break lines as misses, so it understates fit.
-## SketchUp output (on request, from a Claude chat session)
-The Trimble SketchUp connector is available to Claude in chat, **not in CI**, and its plan has a save quota
-(30 saves; check `saves_remaining` in the save result). Use it for the human-facing file, not every build.
-1. `uv run bm skp projects/<site>/specs/<x>-existing.yaml projects/<site>/specs/<x>-proposed.yaml` → code for `build_model` (clean: true).
-2. Add scenes "1 Existing" / "2 Proposed" (hide the other layer), style, model camera; `save_model`.
-3. Download the .skp from the returned URL (follow the redirect) and deliver it. The file's thumbnail shows all
-   layers; the scene tabs switch Existing/Proposed.
-Limits: solid colors only (no textures), no booleans (openings by construction), 30-min idle session timeout.
-Add a `sequence:` block to the proposed spec (steps with caption / remove / install / seconds; `weave` for
-shingles + step flashing course by course; `extras` / `initial_show` / `initial_hide` for partial tear-off).
-`uv run bm animate-sequence projects/<site>/specs/<x>-existing.yaml projects/<site>/specs/<x>-proposed.yaml --out build/<x>-sequence/<x>`
-→ `<x>.mp4` (captioned, any phone) + `<x>.usdz` (same timeline as transform animation, AR-seated).
-Test first with `--test-frames 10,150,236`. Full render ≈ 6 s/frame on 2 CPU cores (Cycles; Workbench/EEVEE
-render blank headless). The sequence is presentation of a recommended order — label it that way when shared.
-**Whole buildings (type: house):** add a `sequence:` block to the house spec — steps with `caption`,
-`objects` (glob patterns on built object names: `slab_*`, `walls`, `attic_*`, `roof`, `soffit`, opening ids such as
-opening (glass, frame, mullions, casing) at a time. Build the model first, then
-The script stops if a step matches nothing and warns about objects in no step. The camera does one elevated
-orbit starting front-left. Cottage A: 271 frames, ≈9 s/frame at 960×540 with 8 samples ≈ 40 min, so run it
-with `nohup … &` and poll the log. Both animators share `src/bmodels/anim_common.py` for captions, which shrink to fit
-the frame width and keep the step counter in sync with the caption on screen.
-- [ ] Local build and CI both PASS.
-- [ ] Overlays reviewed for every elevation you have (front and rear at minimum).
-- [ ] Every opening in the spec appears on an elevation; rejected candidates are listed.
-- [ ] Every `assumed` item has a `basis`; the report's "Assumed" list read and accepted.
-- [ ] Takeoff reconciled to any documented quantity; waste % set.
-- [ ] Handoff states what is not modeled (pergolas, bay roofs, gutters, interior, etc.).
-| Render is a flat grey image; "render not blank" check fails | Workbench/EEVEE need a GPU | Builder uses Cycles CPU; don't change the engine |
-| All cameras look straight down | Track-to constraints not evaluated headless | Cameras use explicit rotation; keep it |
-| Roof boolean produces geometry below grade / volume shrinks | Exact solver on coplanar faces | `house.SOLVER = "MANIFOLD"` |
-| Objects render white though materials are set | Boolean left empty material slot 0 | Use `set_mat()`, never `materials.append()` |
-| Wall missing where a revision cloud or tag crosses | Cloud arcs split the wall band | Add `extra_walls` entry traced from the review PNG |
-| Whole wall run missing on one unit | Dimension/extension lines inside the wall band | Extract the cleaner half and mirror, or add `extra_walls` |
-| False window in a bathroom / garage | Tub, shower or garage-door line | Reject: not on any elevation |
-| Gable "hipped" (shingled triangle at gable end) | Inner roof solid closed the gable end | Inner gable pieces extend 24" past ends (already in `roof_piece`) |
-| Overlay shifted sideways | Wrong centre column | `calibrate.py elev`; don't use mirror-symmetry guesses |
-| Gable panel sf far too high | Interior plane counted | Party-wall plane is excluded in `qto.gable_areas`; check for other interior planes |
-| CI can't push workflow changes from Claude | Token lacks `workflow` scope | Edit `.github/workflows/*` in the GitHub web UI |
-| CI doesn't trigger on workflow-only edits | Path filter says `.yml`, file is `.yaml` | Fix the filter in the web UI |
-Specs and takeoffs are plain files: `git revert <sha>` and push. Build outputs are not committed; previous
-CI artifacts remain downloadable for 30 days. Nothing in this pipeline writes outside the repo.
-| Scanned/raster set, photos-only, multi-story, skewed walls | Michael (owner) | Needs a new extraction method — don't hand-build around it |
-| Units not true mirrors | Michael | Decide: extract both halves (needs `--half all`) or accept documented differences |
-| Documented dimensions disagree with each other | Michael → architect of record | Model per governing sheet, record the conflict in the spec |
-| Check fails and the drawing supports the model | Michael | Update the check's source/tolerance only with a written reason |

-| 2026-09-30 | Claude | Cottage A build-up animation (src/bmodels/animate_house.py): 6 steps, 22.6 s, MP4 + animated USDZ. Walls mesh includes interior partitions traced from AH201 — the caption says so. |
-| 2026-09-27 | Claude | Rake detail AH700/12 (detail mode): 16 components, 2 documented dims pass, drawing-vs-callout warnings on fascia depth and wall sheathing. |

-| 2026-09-27 | Claude (with Michael) | QP Cottage Duplex A (2017 CD set, AH201/AH202/AH500/SH202). Right unit mirrored; 5 false openings rejected; 3 walls under a revision cloud traced manually; roof plan area 3,935.7 vs 3,935 sf documented; overlays 82% / 87%. |
+How every model in this repo is made, whatever the site or model type. Operator commands step by step:

+Purpose: build dimensionally accurate, realistic 3D models of restoration and defect-repair projects (occupied multifamily) from construction drawings, details, specs, and site photos, using Blender driven by Python. Accuracy first, realism second. A model is finished only when every dimension traces to a source or is labeled as assumed, the automated checks pass, and the renders have been looked at.

+1. **Intake.** Inventory every source: sheet number, detail number, revision/date, scale, photo IDs. Read drawings at full resolution (rasterize PDFs with `pdftoppm -r 200+`; crop into details). Note scale bars and "NTS" details.

+2. **Takeoff.** Extract every dimension, member size, spacing, elevation, and count into the model spec. Use actual lumber sizes (2x10 = 1½ × 9¼), not nominal. Never scale an NTS detail. Never infer a dimension from a partial drawing and call it documented.

+3. **Model spec** (`projects/<site>/specs/<area>.yaml`; start a site with `uv run bm new <site>`). The spec is the single source of truth; geometry is never hand-edited in Blender without the spec changing too. Every element carries:
+   - `status: confirmed` — dimension shown on a document (`source` required)
+   - `status: provisional` — derived: scaled from a drawing with a scale bar, or measured from a photo against a known reference (`source` required; note the reference and expected tolerance)
+   - `status: assumed` — not in any document (`basis` required, e.g. "code-minimum", "typical", "massing only")
+   - Document-driven `checks`: counts, overall extents, clear gaps, spacing, elevations — each with its `source`.
+4. **Build.** `uv run bm build <site>[/<spec>] [--realistic]` (bpy, headless). One collection per trade; trades stay separate. Inches in the spec; Blender stores meters, displays imperial.

+5. **Verify.** The builder fails (exit 1) on: missing source/basis, count or extent mismatch, gap mismatch, or a blank render. Then look at the review renders myself — plan, front, side, iso — colored by provenance (green confirmed, yellow provisional, orange assumed). Where a drawing elevation exists, compare the ortho render against it at the same scale. "Checks passed" and "looked right" are both required; report which were done.
+6. **Realism pass** (only after geometry is verified). PBR materials by real product where known; realistic lighting via Cycles. Realism never changes geometry.

+7. **Quantities.** Every house build writes `<name>_takeoff.xlsx` (src/bmodels/qto.py): openings schedule, siding + gable panel net of openings by elevation, casing and corner-board LF, roof area by pitch, squares (waste is a yellow input), ridge/hip/valley/eave/rake LF, and an Elements sheet of stable IDs for trackers. Measured values are blue inputs with method + status; everything derived is a live formula. Reconcile against any documented quantity (Cottage A: plan roof area 3,935.7 vs 3,935 sf on AH202).
+8. **Deliver.** `.blend` (editable), `.glb` (phone/web viewing, carries element metadata), review renders, `report.md`. List every assumed element in the handoff.
+## Plan-set method (proven on QP Cottage A, 2026-09-27)

+- **Calibrate every sheet from its own dimension strings** before measuring anything: find the tick marks of a long dimension and compute pt/ft (AH201: 39'-0" ticks 702 pt apart = 18.0 pt/ft = true 1/4"). Never trust the title-block scale alone.

+- **Rasterize at an exact scale** (2 px/in plans, 1–2 px/in elevations). Walls drawn as hollow outlines are found as thin enclosed white cores (half-width 2.5–7.5 px); window glazing splits the band into strips under 2.3 px half-width.
+- **Every extracted opening must appear on an elevation** or it is rejected (tubs, showers, garage-door lines and revision clouds all produce false openings). Record rejected candidates in the spec.
+- **Revision clouds and tags break linework** — look for missing wall where a cloud crosses, trace it manually, and add it as an `extra_walls` entry with its reason.
+- **Mirror-image units:** extract the cleaner half and mirror, but first measure the match (Cottage A: 94% of walls within 1½").
+- **Roofs:** union of convex hip/gable pieces taken from the eave outline on the roof plan; verify predicted ridge/hip positions against the drawn ones and ridge heights against elevations.

+- **Walls are built boolean-free** (rectangle decomposition, openings cut by box splitting). Roof unions use Blender's **Manifold** boolean solver — the Exact solver fails on the coplanar faces that roofs inevitably have.
+- **Overlay check:** `src/bmodels/overlay.py` renders the model orthographically at the drawing's scale and overlays it on the elevation; report the edge-agreement % and look at the image.
+- **detail** — one construction section (rake, eave, balcony edge, window head) as callout-sized components swept along a short path; 1/16" intent. `src/bmodels/detail.py`.
+- **house** — plan-extracted shell (walls, openings, roof) + quantity takeoff. `src/bmodels/house.py`, `src/bmodels/qto.py`.

+- **room** — interior shell + furniture + lighting from a photo or sketch (`projects/<site>/specs/room-*.yaml`, `src/bmodels/room.py`). Photo-only, so nothing can be `confirmed`: every group is `provisional` (visible, sized from a reference) or `assumed`. Checks are internal consistency (body corners match the spec, clearances, footprints don't overlap), not accuracy to the real room. `src/bmodels/build.py` hands room specs to `room.py` (checks + review renders only, so CI needs no workflow change). Run `uv run bm room projects/room-living-kitchen/specs/room-living-kitchen.yaml [--only review_iso,photomatch_night] [--no-render]`; the full render set is ~25 min on 4 CPU cores.
+- **element / building** — not built yet: parametric components (balcony, stair) and multi-level buildings with repeated units.
+All types share: provenance on every element, failing checks, CI rebuild.

+- Never present an assumed or provisional element as documented. Review renders always show provenance colors; realistic renders shared outside the team must carry a note if any assumed elements are visible.

+- Photos: state the reference object used for scale (brick course, CMU, door, siding exposure, known member size), the camera angle limits, and the resulting tolerance. Photo-only geometry is at best `provisional`.
+- Conflicts between sources (drawing vs. photo vs. spec): model per the governing document, flag the conflict in the report — don't average or silently pick.
+- Existing-conditions models (defect repair) and proposed-repair models are separate scenes or separate specs. Don't merge them.
+- Models are illustrative/coordination tools, not contract documents. Any render used in a scope, PCO, or resident notice gets that label.

+Resident notices (what's happening at their unit), access and sequencing diagrams, protection/staging/egress layouts, and PCO backup showing concealed conditions. For these, include the relevant occupied-building elements (egress paths, protection, staging area, work zone) as their own collection, marked by source like everything else.
+- `uv sync` installs Python 3.11 and the locked `bpy==5.0.1` (see `pyproject.toml`); always run Python as `uv run python …`; build + checks for a small spec run in seconds.
+- Headless has no GPU: **Workbench and EEVEE render blank frames** — use Cycles on CPU only. Cameras need explicit rotation (track-to constraints are not evaluated before headless renders).
+- Exports confirmed working: .blend, .glb, .obj, .stl, .fbx, .usdz. SVG import add-on present. IFC (Bonsai) not installed — unverified.
+- Cycles realistic render: ~2 min for 4 review views + 1 realistic view at 1600×1200 on 2 CPU cores. EEVEE took 45 s for a trivial scene and still returned blank.

+Ask once, batched, only for what can't be read from the documents (e.g. a missing detail, which revision governs). Otherwise take the next step and mark assumptions. Don't claim a model is accurate beyond what its sources support.
+# Runbook: Drawing set → verified Blender model + quantity takeoff
+**Owner:** Michael Colenso | **Frequency:** As needed (one run per building / drawing set)
+**Scope today:** vector-PDF plan sets (CAD-plotted). Single-story, orthogonal walls, hip/gable roofs.
+**Not yet supported:** scanned/raster drawings, photos or field measurements as geometry sources,
+multi-story, curved or skewed walls. Don't force those through this pipeline — flag them.
+Turn a drawing set into (1) a Blender model whose geometry is checked against the drawings, (2) a
+quantity takeoff workbook, and (3) review renders — every element tagged with the sheet it came
+from and whether it is **documented**, **provisional** (measured from a drawing at a verified
+scale) or **assumed**. The model is a coordination/estimating tool, not a contract document.
+Time for a first building like Cottage A: ~2–3 h of operator time; builds take ~2 min
+(review renders) or ~6 min (with realistic renders) on 2 CPU cores.
+- [ ] Python **3.11 exactly** (bpy 5.0.x wheels are cp311 only). Linux or macOS. No GPU needed.
+- [ ] The drawing set as a **vector** PDF. Test: `pdftotext -f N -l N set.pdf - | head` returns dimension
+      text such as `39-0`. If it returns nothing, the set is scanned — stop (see Escalation).
+- [ ] Sheets needed: dimensioned floor plan, roof plan, all exterior elevations, window/door schedule,
+      and the sheet that states plate/truss-bearing height (elevation or framing plan).
+Paths below are from the repo root. `PDF=sources/<project>.pdf` throughout.
+uv sync --group pdf --group vision     # downloads Python 3.11 + the locked deps into .venv
+mkdir -p sources takeoff && cp /path/to/set.pdf sources/<project>.pdf   # sources/ is git-ignored
+**If it fails:** on Linux install `libx11-6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxi6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libice6 libgl1`.
+pdftoppm -r 72 -f <page> -l <page> -png $PDF preview    # at 72 dpi, 1 pixel = 1 PDF point
+**Expected:** each page's own sheet number (title block) and drawing titles; find the floor plan, roof plan,
+elevations and schedules. A page with `-` and no titles has no text layer (raster) — those sheets can't be
+extracted. The cover/index page may show a referenced sheet number instead of its own.
+Record each sheet in the spec's `sources:` list (sheet number, title, revision/date).
+**If it fails:** no text on the plan/roof/elevation pages → scanned set → stop (Escalation).
+### Step 3 — Calibrate the plan sheet from its own dimensions
+uv run bm calibrate scale $PDF --page <plan page> --text "<overall dim, e.g. 78-0>" --feet 78
+uv run bm calibrate scale $PDF --page <plan page> --text "<another dim, e.g. 39-0>" --feet 39
+**Expected:** both give the same pt/ft (Cottage A: 18.000 = ¼"). Must agree within 0.1%.
+**If it fails:** "no bracketing ticks" → the string uses dots/arrows, try another string. Disagreement →
+one string is not-to-scale or mislabeled; use strings that agree and note it.
+### Step 4 — Find the extraction window and origin
+1. Open `preview-*.png` from Step 2 (pixels = points). Read the plan's bounding box in points → `--clip x0,y0,x1,y1`
+   (include the building, exclude title block and schedules).
+2. Centre (party wall / symmetry line) from the overall-width ticks printed in Step 3:
+3. `--rear-px` = `(rear wall face y in points − clip y0) × 24 / pt_per_ft`. Pick the rear face of the section
+(walls black, window candidates orange `W#`, door candidates blue `D#`, labelled with X,Y in inches).
+Use `--half right` only for mirror-image units (see Step 6); otherwise `--half all` is not implemented yet — escalate.
+**If it fails:** walls missing in the review image → see Troubleshooting (clouds, tags, dimension clutter).
+### Step 6 — Review the extraction (do not skip)
+- [ ] **Mirror check** (duplexes): confirm the two units are true mirrors before using `--half`. Look at the plan;
+      if in doubt, escalate — Cottage A measured 94% of walls within 1½".
+- [ ] **Every opening candidate must appear on an elevation.** For each W#/D#, find it on the matching
+      elevation; accept (copy to spec `openings:`) or reject (list in a spec comment with reason).
+      Typical false candidates: tubs/showers, garage-door lines, revision clouds, the party-wall FEC cabinet.
+- [ ] **Holes:** look for walls missing under revision clouds, tags or text. Add each as `extra_walls:` with
+1. Elevation scale: `calibrate.py scale` on an elevation string or use the sheet's stated scale (Cottage A AH500: 9 pt/ft).
+2. **Plate height** from the documented elevations (FF and truss-bearing lines) → `plate_height_in` (documented).
+3. **Window/door heads and sills**: measure on the elevation (see `src/bmodels/overlay.py` raster at 1 px/in) → provisional.
+   Nominal sizes come from the window schedule → put the mark (`mark: A`) on each opening.
+   python src/bmodels/calibrate.py outline $PDF --page <roof plan page> --clip <roof clip> --pt-per-ft <pt/ft> \
+   Take the closed loop of segments (ignore stray section-cut lines drawn at the same weight). Convert Y to the
+   plan frame (Cottage A: roof Y − 2.0 ft, because the rear eave sits 2'-0" behind the rear wall).
+5. **Roof pieces:** decompose the outline into rectangles: one `hip` per main mass, `gable` for each gable with
+   `ridge: x|y` and its gable end at the outline edge. Pitches from the roof plan (documented). Then confirm the
+   model's predicted ridge/hip positions land on the drawn ridge/hip lines (Cottage A: within 0.4').
+6. Eave height (`eave_surface_z_in`) and soffit from the elevation → provisional.
+### Step 8 — Write the spec and checks
+Create the site with `uv run bm new <site>` (once per project), copy `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-cottage-a.yaml` → `projects/<site>/specs/<project>.yaml` and fill it in. Required checks:
+- wall extents vs overall dimension strings (documented),
+- `qto_checks.plan_area_sf` if the set states a roof area anywhere (venting calcs often do).
+uv run bm build <site>/<project>              # ~2 min, review renders
+uv run bm build <site>/<project> --realistic  # ~6 min, adds hero renders
+**Expected:** `**PASS** — n/n checks`, exit code 0, and in `build/<site>/<project>/`: `.blend`, `.glb`,
+**If it fails:** the report names the failing check — fix the spec, never loosen a tolerance to pass.
+### Step 10 — Overlay the model on the elevations
+uv run bm calibrate elev $PDF --page <elev page> --clip <elevation clip> --pt-per-ft <pt/ft> \
+**Expected:** ≥ 80% edge agreement (Cottage A: front 82%, rear 87%) **and** a visual check that windows, doors,
+eaves, ridges and gables sit on the drawing's lines. The % alone is not proof.
+**If it fails:** misaligned horizontally → wrong `--center-col` (re-run `calibrate.py elev`); an element off →
+fix that element in the spec; `side` views need the building's Y-centre (not automated yet).
+- [ ] Opening counts per elevation match the drawings.
+- [ ] Any documented quantity reconciles (roof area, window count).
+- [ ] Set the **roof waste %** (yellow cell) to your standard.
+- [ ] Sanity-check gable panel sf per elevation against a hand estimate (a known past bug counted an interior plane).
+### Step 12 — Commit and let CI rebuild
+git add projects/<site> && git commit -m "Model <project>" && git push
+**Expected:** Actions run "Build & verify models" goes green; the job summary shows each `report.md`;
+**If it fails:** open the run → "Build, verify, render" step log → the failing check is printed.
+## Detail mode (sections: rake, eave, balcony edge, window head …)
+Use when the source is a **section detail**, not a plan. Spec type `detail` (example: `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-rake-ah700-12.yaml`).
+1. **Pick a true section at a stated scale.** Reject NTS / perspective sketches for geometry (AT401/4 rake is NTS — used only for sequence).
+2. **Verify the detail scale** from a dimension string inside the detail:
+   `uv run bm calibrate scale $PDF --page 8 --text "1-6" --feet 1.5` (AH700/12: 106.5 pt/ft vs 108 nominal — sheet plots 1.4% small; always use the measured value).
+3. **Section frame:** X horizontal from a named face (e.g. fascia outer face = 0), Z plumb from a named plane (e.g. underside of roof sheathing = 0). Write that in the spec header.

+4. **One component per callout**, sized by the callout's **actual** dimensions (5/4x10 = 1 × 9¼; 1x6 = ¾ × 5½), positioned from the drawing. Thicknesses stated elsewhere (wall types, structural notes) cite that sheet. Anything drawn but not called out = provisional with a `basis`; anything not drawn = assumed.

+5. **Checks:** every dimension string in the detail as a `between:` check (hard); measured drawn sizes as `drawn:` checks (warn only — they test the *drawing* against its callouts; a ⚠️ means the drawing and the callout disagree, e.g. fascia drawn 10.1" deep vs 9¼" called out).
+6. `path:` length and `pitch:` (rake follows the roof slope). `peel:` / `cutaway_step_in:` are presentation only — the near end stays a true section.
+7. Build with `--realistic` for the labeled cutaway; then

+ `uv run bm detail-overlay build///.blend --pdf $PDF --page

--clip --pt-per-ft --origin-pt --out build///overlay_section.png`
+   Judge by eye: the % counts model outline beyond the detail's break lines as misses, so it understates fit.
+## SketchUp output (on request, from a Claude chat session)
+The Trimble SketchUp connector is available to Claude in chat, **not in CI**, and its plan has a save quota
+(30 saves; check `saves_remaining` in the save result). Use it for the human-facing file, not every build.
+1. `uv run bm skp projects/<site>/specs/<x>-existing.yaml projects/<site>/specs/<x>-proposed.yaml` → code for `build_model` (clean: true).
+2. Add scenes "1 Existing" / "2 Proposed" (hide the other layer), style, model camera; `save_model`.
+3. Download the .skp from the returned URL (follow the redirect) and deliver it. The file's thumbnail shows all
+   layers; the scene tabs switch Existing/Proposed.
+Limits: solid colors only (no textures), no booleans (openings by construction), 30-min idle session timeout.
+Add a `sequence:` block to the proposed spec (steps with caption / remove / install / seconds; `weave` for
+shingles + step flashing course by course; `extras` / `initial_show` / `initial_hide` for partial tear-off).
+`uv run bm animate-sequence projects/<site>/specs/<x>-existing.yaml projects/<site>/specs/<x>-proposed.yaml --out build/<x>-sequence/<x>`
+→ `<x>.mp4` (captioned, any phone) + `<x>.usdz` (same timeline as transform animation, AR-seated).
+Test first with `--test-frames 10,150,236`. Full render ≈ 6 s/frame on 2 CPU cores (Cycles; Workbench/EEVEE
+render blank headless). The sequence is presentation of a recommended order — label it that way when shared.
+**Whole buildings (type: house):** add a `sequence:` block to the house spec — steps with `caption`,
+`objects` (glob patterns on built object names: `slab_*`, `walls`, `attic_*`, `roof`, `soffit`, opening ids such as
+opening (glass, frame, mullions, casing) at a time. Build the model first, then
+The script stops if a step matches nothing and warns about objects in no step. The camera does one elevated
+orbit starting front-left. Cottage A: 271 frames, ≈9 s/frame at 960×540 with 8 samples ≈ 40 min, so run it
+with `nohup … &` and poll the log. Both animators share `src/bmodels/anim_common.py` for captions, which shrink to fit
+the frame width and keep the step counter in sync with the caption on screen.
+- [ ] Local build and CI both PASS.
+- [ ] Overlays reviewed for every elevation you have (front and rear at minimum).
+- [ ] Every opening in the spec appears on an elevation; rejected candidates are listed.
+- [ ] Every `assumed` item has a `basis`; the report's "Assumed" list read and accepted.
+- [ ] Takeoff reconciled to any documented quantity; waste % set.
+- [ ] Handoff states what is not modeled (pergolas, bay roofs, gutters, interior, etc.).
+| Render is a flat grey image; "render not blank" check fails | Workbench/EEVEE need a GPU | Builder uses Cycles CPU; don't change the engine |
+| All cameras look straight down | Track-to constraints not evaluated headless | Cameras use explicit rotation; keep it |
+| Roof boolean produces geometry below grade / volume shrinks | Exact solver on coplanar faces | `house.SOLVER = "MANIFOLD"` |
+| Objects render white though materials are set | Boolean left empty material slot 0 | Use `set_mat()`, never `materials.append()` |
+| Wall missing where a revision cloud or tag crosses | Cloud arcs split the wall band | Add `extra_walls` entry traced from the review PNG |
+| Whole wall run missing on one unit | Dimension/extension lines inside the wall band | Extract the cleaner half and mirror, or add `extra_walls` |
+| False window in a bathroom / garage | Tub, shower or garage-door line | Reject: not on any elevation |
+| Gable "hipped" (shingled triangle at gable end) | Inner roof solid closed the gable end | Inner gable pieces extend 24" past ends (already in `roof_piece`) |
+| Overlay shifted sideways | Wrong centre column | `calibrate.py elev`; don't use mirror-symmetry guesses |
+| Gable panel sf far too high | Interior plane counted | Party-wall plane is excluded in `qto.gable_areas`; check for other interior planes |

+| Units not true mirrors | Michael | Decide: extract both halves (needs `--half all`) or accept documented differences |

+| Check fails and the drawing supports the model | Michael | Update the check's source/tolerance only with a written reason |

# Blender models of construction projects

Dimensionally accurate, provenance-tracked 3D models of restoration and defect-repair work in occupied
multifamily buildings, built headless in Blender from construction drawings, details, specs and site photos.
Accuracy first, realism second: every dimension traces to a source or is labeled assumed, automated checks
must pass, and the renders get looked at. How models are made: **[docs/METHOD.md](docs/METHOD.md)** ·
step-by-step commands: **[docs/RUNBOOK.md](docs/RUNBOOK.md)**.

## Quickstart

```bash
uv sync                                   # Python 3.11 + locked bpy 5.0.1, PyMuPDF, OpenCV (one environment)
uvx pre-commit install                    # once per clone: blocks oversized or unsourced commits
uv run bm list                            # sites, specs, products
uv run bm new <site> --type detail        # start a project from templates/project/
uv run bm build <site>                    # build + verify every spec of a site (or <site>/<spec>)
uv run bm check                           # provenance, metadata, large files, links, tests
```

Linux needs the X11 libraries bpy links against:
`sudo apt-get install libx11-6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxi6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libice6 libgl1`.
Always run Python through uv (`uv run python …`, `uv run bm …`). Node pieces (browser viewers, Playwright
films) use npm inside their product folder.

## Layout

```
projects/<site>/
  project.yaml               name, address, building type, scope, release tag prefix
  sources/manifest.json      inventory of drawings and photos (the files themselves stay out of git)
  specs/*.yaml               spec-driven models: detail | house | room | element  → `bm build`
  takeoff/                   extracted plan data the specs read
  products/<name>/           bespoke pipelines (films, viewers, bid models) + product.yaml steps → `bm run`
  deliverables/<name>/       what gets handed over: READMEs, previews; large files via Releases
src/bmodels/                 the shared toolkit and the `bm` CLI
templates/project/           what `bm new` copies
assets/                      shared CC0 assets (HDRIs)
render/                      saved-scene shot catalog for the render-scenes workflow
docs/                        METHOD.md, RUNBOOK.md
```

## Sites

| Site | Name | Specs | Products |
|---|---|---|---|
| [field-parapet](projects/field-parapet/) | Field parapet (site photo P1) | field-parapet-existing, field-parapet-proposed | — |
| [highland](projects/highland/) | 200 W. Highland condominiums | — | exterior, installation, repipe, walkthrough, water |
| [meydenbauer-b](projects/meydenbauer-b/) | 101 Meydenbauer, Building B | — | underslab |
| [qp-cottage-a](projects/qp-cottage-a/) | Quail Park of Lynnwood — Cottage Duplex A | qp-cottage-a, qp-rake-ah700-12 | — |
| [room-living-kitchen](projects/room-living-kitchen/) | Living room / kitchen (occupied apartment) | room-living-kitchen | — |
| [sample](projects/sample/) | SAMPLE — pipeline fixture (not a real project) | sample-bay | — |

Regenerate with `uv run bm list --markdown`. Highlights: Highland
[archviz walkthrough](projects/highland/deliverables/archviz/README.md),
[installation film](projects/highland/deliverables/installation/README.md),
[cinema shot list](projects/highland/products/walkthrough/CINEMA.md) (film not published);
Meydenbauer [bid model, realism views and 4D films](projects/meydenbauer-b/deliverables/underslab/README.md).

## Commands

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `bm build [path \| site \| site/spec] [--realistic] [--changed BASE]` | build, verify and render specs → `build/<site>/<spec>/` |
| `bm run <site>/<product> <step> [args]` | run a step declared in `product.yaml` |
| `bm check [--staged \| --base REF]` · `bm check-products` | repo checks · every product's `check` step |
| `bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>` · `bm assets pull\|verify <manifest>` | large outputs to/from GitHub Releases |
| `bm calibrate`, `extract`, `overlay`, `detail-overlay` | drawing intake (see the runbook) |
| `bm render`, `render-plan`, `animate-house`, `animate-sequence`, `room`, `skp`, `usdz`, `audit-blends` | renders, sequences, exports, scene audit |

## Large files

New files over 1 MB (MP4, .blend, ZIP, EXR, GLB, big GIF/HTML) go to **GitHub Releases**, not git:
`uv run bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>` uploads them, records sha256 in the product's
`release-assets.json`, keeps the local copies out of git and prints README links; `uv run bm assets pull
<manifest>` restores them. `bm check` (pre-commit and CI) rejects new oversized files. Files already in Git LFS
stay there and may be updated; nothing new goes to LFS.

## CI

| Workflow | When | What |
|---|---|---|
| `build-models` | specs, takeoff, products, `src/`, lock change | `bm build --changed` (every spec when code or the lock changes) and `bm check-products`; reports in the job summary, `build/` as artifact |
| `checks` | every PR and push to main | `bm check --base …` (provenance, metadata, large files, links, tests) and `bm audit-blends` |
| `render-scenes` | `render/`, renderer or project changes | render each shot in `render/scenes.json` on CPU and validate the pixels |
| `highland-*` | manual | Highland native film, archviz review and preview renders |

Every workflow sets up through `.github/actions/setup-blender-env` (apt libraries, setup-uv cached on
`uv.lock`, `uv sync --frozen`). Pushes from a local clone can change workflow files; cloud agent tokens
without the `workflow` scope cannot.

# CLAUDE.md

Provenance-tracked Blender models of construction projects. Method: `docs/METHOD.md` (read before modeling).
Commands step by step: `docs/RUNBOOK.md`. Layout and tools: `README.md`.

## Non-negotiables

- Every element is `confirmed` (with `source`), `provisional` (with `source` + reference and tolerance) or
  `assumed` (with `basis`). Never present assumed or provisional geometry as documented.
- The spec is the source of truth; never hand-edit geometry without changing the spec.
- Actual lumber sizes (2x10 = 1½ × 9¼), never nominal. Never scale an NTS detail. Calibrate every sheet
  from its own dimension strings, not the title-block scale.
- Conflicting sources: model the governing document and flag the conflict; don't average or pick silently.
- Existing-conditions and proposed-repair models are separate specs/scenes.
- "Checks passed" and "looked at the renders" are both required; say which you did.
- Renders used in a scope, PCO or resident notice carry "illustrative, not a contract document".

## Environment

- **uv only.** `uv sync`, then `uv run bm …` / `uv run python …`. Never `pip`, never a bare venv, never
  `requirements.txt`. Add dependencies with `uv add` (or `uv add --group <pdf|vision|audio|dev>`).
- The bpy 5.0.1 wheel mislabels its tag, so a syncing `uv run` reinstalls bpy each time. In scripts and
  parallel workers: `uv sync --frozen` once, then `uv run --no-sync …`.
- Headless Blender has no GPU: Cycles on CPU only (Workbench/EEVEE render blank). Cameras need explicit
  rotation. This laptop (WSL, Iris Xe) cannot import bpy without the X11 libs and has no GPU or Unreal:
  bpy builds are verified by CI; GPU renders run on RunPod (`products/*/runpod_*.sh`).

## Where work goes

- New project: `uv run bm new <site> [--type element|detail]`, then fill `project.yaml` and
  `sources/manifest.json`. Source PDFs/photos stay in `sources/` (git-ignored, only the manifest is committed).
- Spec-driven models: `projects/<site>/specs/*.yaml`, built with `bm build <site>[/<spec>]`.
- Anything bespoke (films, viewers, bid models): `projects/<site>/products/<name>/` with a `product.yaml`
  listing `steps` (one must be `check`: fast, CPU, no source PDFs; CI runs it). Run with `bm run`.
- Shared code goes in `src/bmodels/`, never imported across sites through `sys.path`. Shared CC0 assets go
  in `assets/`. Repo root in scripts: `from bmodels.paths import ROOT`, not counted `parents[N]`.
- Handover files: `projects/<site>/deliverables/<name>/`.

## Large files

New files over 1 MB go to GitHub Releases: `bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>`, then link the printed
URLs from the deliverable README. Never add new files to Git LFS. `bm check --staged` (pre-commit) and CI
block oversized commits; exceptions go in `.bmcheck.yaml` with a reason.

## Before you finish

- `uv run bm check` (and `bm check-products` if you touched a product) must pass.
- Moving files: `git mv`, keep markdown links relative and valid (`bm check` verifies them), and run
  `bm audit-blends` in CI for any moved `.blend`.
- Commit or push only when asked; branch first if on `main`.

## Working style

Ask once, batched, only for what the documents can't answer (a missing detail, which revision governs).
Otherwise take the next step and mark assumptions. Don't claim accuracy beyond what the sources support.

-- **Revision clouds and tags break linework** — look for missing wall where a cloud crosses, trace it manually, and add it as an `extra_walls` entry with its reason.
-- **Mirror-image units:** extract the cleaner half and mirror, but first measure the match (Cottage A: 94% of walls within 1½").
-- **Roofs:** union of convex hip/gable pieces taken from the eave outline on the roof plan; verify predicted ridge/hip positions against the drawn ones and ridge heights against elevations.

# Blender Project — Instructions

Highland cinematic film: [shot list and rebuild](projects/highland/products/walkthrough/CINEMA.md) (the rendered film is not published in this repo).

Highland architectural walkthrough: [upgraded full film, phone preview and Blender scene](projects/highland/deliverables/archviz/README.md).

Highland installation: [90-second installation animation and downloads](projects/highland/deliverables/installation/README.md) · [source project and editable-model setup](projects/highland/products/installation/README.md).

Purpose: build dimensionally accurate, realistic 3D models of Michael's restoration and defect-repair projects (occupied multifamily) from construction drawings, details, specs, and site photos, using Blender driven by Python. Accuracy first, realism second. A model is finished only when every dimension traces to a source or is labeled as assumed, the automated checks pass, and the renders have been looked at.

Operator procedure with exact commands: **RUNBOOK.md**.

Saved-model rendering: [GitHub Actions workflow, shot catalog and operating guide](render/README.md).

## Pipeline (always in this order)

1. **Intake.** Inventory every source: sheet number, detail number, revision/date, scale, photo IDs. Read drawings at full resolution (rasterize PDFs with `pdftoppm -r 200+`; crop into details). Note scale bars and "NTS" details.
2. **Takeoff.** Extract every dimension, member size, spacing, elevation, and count into the model spec. Use actual lumber sizes (2x10 = 1½ × 9¼), not nominal. Never scale an NTS detail. Never infer a dimension from a partial drawing and call it documented.
3. **Model spec** (`projects/<site>/specs/<area>.yaml`; start a site with `uv run bm new <site>`). The spec is the single source of truth; geometry is never hand-edited in Blender without the spec changing too. Every element carries:
   - `status: confirmed` — dimension shown on a document (`source` required)
   - `status: provisional` — derived: scaled from a drawing with a scale bar, or measured from a photo against a known reference (`source` required; note the reference and expected tolerance)
   - `status: assumed` — not in any document (`basis` required, e.g. "code-minimum", "typical", "massing only")
   - Document-driven `checks`: counts, overall extents, clear gaps, spacing, elevations — each with its `source`.
4. **Build.** `uv run bm build <site>[/<spec>] [--realistic]` (bpy, headless). One collection per trade; trades stay separate. Inches in the spec; Blender stores meters, displays imperial.
5. **Verify.** The builder fails (exit 1) on: missing source/basis, count or extent mismatch, gap mismatch, or a blank render. Then look at the review renders myself — plan, front, side, iso — colored by provenance (green confirmed, yellow provisional, orange assumed). Where a drawing elevation exists, compare the ortho render against it at the same scale. "Checks passed" and "looked right" are both required; report which were done.
6. **Realism pass** (only after geometry is verified). PBR materials by real product where known; realistic lighting via Cycles. Realism never changes geometry.
7. **Quantities.** Every house build writes `<name>_takeoff.xlsx` (src/bmodels/qto.py): openings schedule, siding + gable panel net of openings by elevation, casing and corner-board LF, roof area by pitch, squares (waste is a yellow input), ridge/hip/valley/eave/rake LF, and an Elements sheet of stable IDs for trackers. Measured values are blue inputs with method + status; everything derived is a live formula. Reconcile against any documented quantity (Cottage A: plan roof area 3,935.7 vs 3,935 sf on AH202).
8. **Deliver.** `.blend` (editable), `.glb` (phone/web viewing, carries element metadata), review renders, `report.md`. List every assumed element in the handoff.

## Plan-set method (proven on QP Cottage A, 2026-09-27)

- **Calibrate every sheet from its own dimension strings** before measuring anything: find the tick marks of a long dimension and compute pt/ft (AH201: 39'-0" ticks 702 pt apart = 18.0 pt/ft = true 1/4"). Never trust the title-block scale alone.
- **Rasterize at an exact scale** (2 px/in plans, 1–2 px/in elevations). Walls drawn as hollow outlines are found as thin enclosed white cores (half-width 2.5–7.5 px); window glazing splits the band into strips under 2.3 px half-width.
- **Every extracted opening must appear on an elevation** or it is rejected (tubs, showers, garage-door lines and revision clouds all produce false openings). Record rejected candidates in the spec.
- **Revision clouds and tags break linework** — look for missing wall where a cloud crosses, trace it manually, and add it as an `extra_walls` entry with its reason.
- **Mirror-image units:** extract the cleaner half and mirror, but first measure the match (Cottage A: 94% of walls within 1½").
- **Roofs:** union of convex hip/gable pieces taken from the eave outline on the roof plan; verify predicted ridge/hip positions against the drawn ones and ridge heights against elevations.
- **Walls are built boolean-free** (rectangle decomposition, openings cut by box splitting). Roof unions use Blender's **Manifold** boolean solver — the Exact solver fails on the coplanar faces that roofs inevitably have.
- **Overlay check:** `src/bmodels/overlay.py` renders the model orthographically at the drawing's scale and overlays it on the elevation; report the edge-agreement % and look at the image.

## Model types

- **detail** — one construction section (rake, eave, balcony edge, window head) as callout-sized components swept along a short path; 1/16" intent. `src/bmodels/detail.py`.
- **house** — plan-extracted shell (walls, openings, roof) + quantity takeoff. `src/bmodels/house.py`, `src/bmodels/qto.py`.
- **room** — interior shell + furniture + lighting from a photo or sketch (`projects/<site>/specs/room-*.yaml`, `src/bmodels/room.py`). Photo-only, so nothing can be `confirmed`: every group is `provisional` (visible, sized from a reference) or `assumed`. Checks are internal consistency (body corners match the spec, clearances, footprints don't overlap), not accuracy to the real room. `src/bmodels/build.py` hands room specs to `room.py` (checks + review renders only, so CI needs no workflow change). Run `uv run bm room projects/room-living-kitchen/specs/room-living-kitchen.yaml [--only review_iso,photomatch_night] [--no-render]`; the full render set is ~25 min on 4 CPU cores.
- **element / building** — not built yet: parametric components (balcony, stair) and multi-level buildings with repeated units.
All types share: provenance on every element, failing checks, CI rebuild.

## Accuracy rules

- Never present an assumed or provisional element as documented. Review renders always show provenance colors; realistic renders shared outside the team must carry a note if any assumed elements are visible.
- Photos: state the reference object used for scale (brick course, CMU, door, siding exposure, known member size), the camera angle limits, and the resulting tolerance. Photo-only geometry is at best `provisional`.
- Conflicts between sources (drawing vs. photo vs. spec): model per the governing document, flag the conflict in the report — don't average or silently pick.
- Existing-conditions models (defect repair) and proposed-repair models are separate scenes or separate specs. Don't merge them.
- Models are illustrative/coordination tools, not contract documents. Any render used in a scope, PCO, or resident notice gets that label.

## Occupied-building use cases

Resident notices (what's happening at their unit), access and sequencing diagrams, protection/staging/egress layouts, and PCO backup showing concealed conditions. For these, include the relevant occupied-building elements (egress paths, protection, staging area, work zone) as their own collection, marked by source like everything else.

## Environment facts (verified 2026-09-27)

- `uv sync` installs Python 3.11 and the locked `bpy==5.0.1` (see `pyproject.toml`); always run Python as `uv run python …`; build + checks for a small spec run in seconds.
- Headless has no GPU: **Workbench and EEVEE render blank frames** — use Cycles on CPU only. Cameras need explicit rotation (track-to constraints are not evaluated before headless renders).
- Exports confirmed working: .blend, .glb, .obj, .stl, .fbx, .usdz. SVG import add-on present. IFC (Bonsai) not installed — unverified.
- Cycles realistic render: ~2 min for 4 review views + 1 realistic view at 1600×1200 on 2 CPU cores. EEVEE took 45 s for a trivial scene and still returned blank.

## Large files

New files over 1 MB (MP4, .blend, ZIP, EXR, GLB, big GIF/HTML) go to **GitHub Releases**, not git:

```bash
uv run bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>     # upload, record sha256 in release-assets.json, print README links
uv run bm assets pull <manifest>                # restore them anywhere, checksum-verified
uvx pre-commit install                          # once per clone: blocks oversized commits locally
```

`bm check` (pre-commit and the `checks` workflow) rejects new oversized files. Files already in Git LFS stay there and may be updated; nothing new goes to LFS.

## CI

Workflow: `.github/workflows/build-models.yaml` (edit it in the GitHub web UI — Claude's token can't write workflow files).

GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/build-models.yml`) rebuilds changed specs on every PR and push to main, fails the PR if any check fails, writes each report to the job summary, and uploads `build/` as an artifact. Claude does the takeoff and spec edits; CI makes the geometry reproducible and blocks unsourced or inconsistent changes.

## Working style

Ask once, batched, only for what can't be read from the documents (e.g. a missing detail, which revision governs). Otherwise take the next step and mark assumptions. Don't claim a model is accurate beyond what its sources support.

# CLAUDE.md

Provenance-tracked Blender models of construction projects. Method: `docs/METHOD.md` (read before modeling).
Commands step by step: `docs/RUNBOOK.md`. Layout and tools: `README.md`.

## Non-negotiables

- Every element is `confirmed` (with `source`), `provisional` (with `source` + reference and tolerance) or
  `assumed` (with `basis`). Never present assumed or provisional geometry as documented.
- The spec is the source of truth; never hand-edit geometry without changing the spec.
- Actual lumber sizes (2x10 = 1½ × 9¼), never nominal. Never scale an NTS detail. Calibrate every sheet
  from its own dimension strings, not the title-block scale.
- Conflicting sources: model the governing document and flag the conflict; don't average or pick silently.
- Existing-conditions and proposed-repair models are separate specs/scenes.
- "Checks passed" and "looked at the renders" are both required; say which you did.
- Renders used in a scope, PCO or resident notice carry "illustrative, not a contract document".

## Environment

- **uv only.** `uv sync`, then `uv run bm …` / `uv run python …`. Never `pip`, never a bare venv, never
  `requirements.txt`. Add dependencies with `uv add` (or `uv add --group <pdf|vision|audio|dev>`).
- The bpy 5.0.1 wheel mislabels its tag, so a syncing `uv run` reinstalls bpy each time. In scripts and
  parallel workers: `uv sync --frozen` once, then `uv run --no-sync …`.
- Headless Blender has no GPU: Cycles on CPU only (Workbench/EEVEE render blank). Cameras need explicit
  rotation. This laptop (WSL, Iris Xe) cannot import bpy without the X11 libs and has no GPU or Unreal:
  bpy builds are verified by CI; GPU renders run on RunPod (`products/*/runpod_*.sh`).

## Where work goes

- New project: `uv run bm new <site> [--type element|detail]`, then fill `project.yaml` and
  `sources/manifest.json`. Source PDFs/photos stay in `sources/` (git-ignored, only the manifest is committed).
- Spec-driven models: `projects/<site>/specs/*.yaml`, built with `bm build <site>[/<spec>]`.
- Anything bespoke (films, viewers, bid models): `projects/<site>/products/<name>/` with a `product.yaml`
  listing `steps` (one must be `check`: fast, CPU, no source PDFs; CI runs it). Run with `bm run`.
- Shared code goes in `src/bmodels/`, never imported across sites through `sys.path`. Shared CC0 assets go
  in `assets/`. Repo root in scripts: `from bmodels.paths import ROOT`, not counted `parents[N]`.
- Handover files: `projects/<site>/deliverables/<name>/`.

## Large files

New files over 1 MB go to GitHub Releases: `bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>`, then link the printed
URLs from the deliverable README. Never add new files to Git LFS. `bm check --staged` (pre-commit) and CI
block oversized commits; exceptions go in `.bmcheck.yaml` with a reason.

## Before you finish

- `uv run bm check` (and `bm check-products` if you touched a product) must pass.
- Moving files: `git mv`, keep markdown links relative and valid (`bm check` verifies them), and run
  `bm audit-blends` in CI for any moved `.blend`.
- Commit or push only when asked; branch first if on `main`.

## Working style

Ask once, batched, only for what the documents can't answer (a missing detail, which revision governs).
Otherwise take the next step and mark assumptions. Don't claim accuracy beyond what the sources support.

### Step 1 — Set up

```bash
git clone https://github.com/michaelcolenso/blender-models && cd blender-models
```

artifact `models-<sha>` contains the build folder (kept 30 days).

- `bm check-products` and `bm audit-blends` — #26;
- the large-file guard — #27.

This adds the one remaining gap. CI installs with `uv sync --frozen`, which uses the lock as written. If someone edits `pyproject.toml` without running `uv lock`, CI would still pass on the stale lock. `checks` now runs `uv lock --check` first.

```bash
uv sync
uvx pre-commit install
```

- Publish existing large deliverables to Releases with `bm publish`. Only new files are covered by the policy today.

"""`bm doctor`: what this machine can and cannot do, and the exact fix for each gap.

Agents should run it first: it explains failures that otherwise surface as deep tracebacks
(bpy missing X11 libraries, LFS pointers instead of files, absent source PDFs, no gh auth).
No bpy import in this process; bpy is probed in a subprocess.
"""
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

from bmodels import project
from bmodels.paths import ROOT

LFS_POINTER = b"version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1"
X11 = "libx11-6 libxrender1 libxfixes3 libxi6 libxext6 libxkbcommon0 libsm6 libice6 libgl1"


def _run(*cmd):
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=120)
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as e:
        return 1, str(e)
    return p.returncode, (p.stdout + p.stderr).strip()


def checks():
    """(name, ok, detail, fix, blocks) — blocks says what fails without it."""
    out = []
    ok = sys.version_info[:2] == (3, 11)
    out.append(("python 3.11", ok, sys.version.split()[0], "uv sync", "everything"))

    code, msg = _run(sys.executable, "-c", "import bpy; print(bpy.app.version_string)")
    detail = msg.splitlines()[-1] if msg else ""
    fix = f"sudo apt-get install -y {X11}" if "lib" in detail and ".so" in detail else "uv sync"
    out.append(("bpy imports", code == 0, detail, fix,
                "bm build, check-products steps that use bpy, renders, audit-blends — CI still runs them"))

    code, msg = _run("uv", "lock", "--check")
    out.append(("uv.lock matches pyproject.toml", code == 0, "" if code == 0 else msg.splitlines()[-1],
                "uv lock && uv sync", "CI (checks workflow)"))

    hook = (ROOT / ".git/hooks/pre-commit")
    out.append(("pre-commit hook", hook.exists() and "pre-commit" in hook.read_text(errors="ignore"), "",
                "uvx pre-commit install", "local large-file/provenance guard (CI still checks)"))

    code, msg = _run("gh", "auth", "status")
    out.append(("gh authenticated", code == 0, "" if code == 0 else msg.splitlines()[0] if msg else "gh missing",
                "gh auth login", "bm publish, bm assets pull (releases), PR/CI inspection"))

    pointers = []
    out_ls = _run("git", "lfs", "ls-files", "-n")
    lfs = shutil.which("git-lfs") is not None
    if lfs and out_ls[0] == 0:
        for f in out_ls[1].splitlines():
            p = ROOT / f
            if p.is_file() and p.read_bytes()[:len(LFS_POINTER)] == LFS_POINTER:
                pointers.append(f)
    else:
        code, files = _run("git", "ls-files", "*.blend", "*.mp4", "*.zip", "*.pdf")
        for f in files.splitlines():
            p = ROOT / f
            if p.is_file() and p.stat().st_size < 200 and p.read_bytes()[:len(LFS_POINTER)] == LFS_POINTER:
                pointers.append(f)
    out.append(("LFS files present (not pointers)", not pointers,
                f"{len(pointers)} pointer files, e.g. {pointers[0]}" if pointers else "",
                "sudo apt-get install -y git-lfs && git lfs pull" if not lfs else "git lfs pull",
                "opening those .blend/.mp4 files, installation asset restore"))

    for tool, blocks in [("ffmpeg", "film encodes and video checks"), ("node", "browser viewers and Playwright films"),
                         ("npm", "viewer bundles")]:
        out.append((f"{tool} on PATH", shutil.which(tool) is not None, "", f"install {tool}", blocks))

    code, _ = _run("nvidia-smi")
    out.append(("NVIDIA GPU", code == 0, "", "use RunPod: products/*/runpod_*.sh",
                "GPU Cycles renders (CPU Cycles still works)"))

    missing = []
    for s in project.sites():
        src = s.dir / "sources"
        files = [p for p in src.glob("**/*") if p.is_file() and p.name != "manifest.json"] if src.exists() else []
        if not files:
            missing.append(s.name)
    out.append(("source drawings/photos present", not missing,
                f"none in sources/ for: {', '.join(missing)}" if missing else "",
                "copy them into projects/<site>/sources/ (never committed)",
                "prepare/extract steps that read PDFs; committed specs and takeoff still build"))
    return out


def main(json_out=False):
    results = checks()
    if json_out:
        import json
        print(json.dumps([{"check": n, "ok": ok, "detail": d, "fix": f, "without_it": b}
                          for n, ok, d, f, b in results], indent=2))
    else:
        for n, ok, d, f, b in results:
            print(f"{'ok  ' if ok else 'MISS'}  {n}" + (f" — {d}" if d else ""))
            if not ok:
                print(f"        fix: {f}\n        without it: {b}")
    required = {"python 3.11", "uv.lock matches pyproject.toml"}
    return 1 if any(not ok and n in required for n, ok, *_ in results) else 0

    code, msg = _run("uv", "lock", "--check")
    out.append(("uv.lock matches pyproject.toml", code == 0, "" if code == 0 else msg.splitlines()[-1],
                "uv lock && uv sync", "CI (checks workflow)"))

    hook = (ROOT / ".git/hooks/pre-commit")
    out.append(("pre-commit hook", hook.exists() and "pre-commit" in hook.read_text(errors="ignore"), "",

    code, msg = _run("gh", "auth", "status")
    out.append(("gh authenticated", code == 0, "" if code == 0 else msg.splitlines()[0] if msg else "gh missing",

        for f in out_ls[1].splitlines():
            p = ROOT / f
            if p.is_file() and p.read_bytes()[:len(LFS_POINTER)] == LFS_POINTER:
                pointers.append(f)
    else:
        code, files = _run("git", "ls-files", "*.blend", "*.mp4", "*.zip", "*.pdf")
        for f in files.splitlines():
            p = ROOT / f
            if p.is_file() and p.stat().st_size < 200 and p.read_bytes()[:len(LFS_POINTER)] == LFS_POINTER:
                pointers.append(f)
    out.append(("LFS files present (not pointers)", not pointers,
                f"{len(pointers)} pointer files, e.g. {pointers[0]}" if pointers else "",
                "sudo apt-get install -y git-lfs && git lfs pull" if not lfs else "git lfs pull",
                "opening those .blend/.mp4 files, installation asset restore"))

    for tool, blocks in [("ffmpeg", "film encodes and video checks"), ("node", "browser viewers and Playwright films"),

        out.append((f"{tool} on PATH", shutil.which(tool) is not None, "", f"install {tool}", blocks))

    code, _ = _run("nvidia-smi")
    out.append(("NVIDIA GPU", code == 0, "", "use RunPod: products/*/runpod_*.sh",
                "GPU Cycles renders (CPU Cycles still works)"))

    missing = []
    for s in project.sites():
        src = s.dir / "sources"
        files = [p for p in src.glob("**/*") if p.is_file() and p.name != "manifest.json"] if src.exists() else []
        if not files:

                f"none in sources/ for: {', '.join(missing)}" if missing else "",
                "copy them into projects/<site>/sources/ (never committed)",
                "prepare/extract steps that read PDFs; committed specs and takeoff still build"))
    return out


def main(json_out=False):
    results = checks()
    if json_out:
        import json
        print(json.dumps([{"check": n, "ok": ok, "detail": d, "fix": f, "without_it": b}
                          for n, ok, d, f, b in results], indent=2))
    else:
        for n, ok, d, f, b in results:

            if not ok:

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md

Provenance-tracked Blender models of construction projects. Method: `docs/METHOD.md` (read before modeling).
Commands step by step: `docs/RUNBOOK.md`. Layout and tools: `README.md`.

## Non-negotiables

- Every element is `confirmed` (with `source`), `provisional` (with `source` + reference and tolerance) or
  `assumed` (with `basis`). Never present assumed or provisional geometry as documented.
- The spec is the source of truth; never hand-edit geometry without changing the spec.
- Actual lumber sizes (2x10 = 1½ × 9¼), never nominal. Never scale an NTS detail. Calibrate every sheet
  from its own dimension strings, not the title-block scale.
- Conflicting sources: model the governing document and flag the conflict; don't average or pick silently.
- Existing-conditions and proposed-repair models are separate specs/scenes.
- "Checks passed" and "looked at the renders" are both required; say which you did.
- Renders used in a scope, PCO or resident notice carry "illustrative, not a contract document".

## Environment

- **uv only.** `uv sync`, then `uv run bm …` / `uv run python …`. Never `pip`, never a bare venv, never
  `requirements.txt`. Add dependencies with `uv add` (or `uv add --group <pdf|vision|audio|dev>`).
- The bpy 5.0.1 wheel mislabels its tag, so a syncing `uv run` reinstalls bpy each time. In scripts and
  parallel workers: `uv sync --frozen` once, then `uv run --no-sync …`.
- Headless Blender has no GPU: Cycles on CPU only (Workbench/EEVEE render blank). Cameras need explicit
  rotation. This laptop (WSL, Iris Xe) cannot import bpy without the X11 libs and has no GPU or Unreal:
  bpy builds are verified by CI; GPU renders run on RunPod (`products/*/runpod_*.sh`).

## Where work goes

- New project: `uv run bm new <site> [--type element|detail]`, then fill `project.yaml` and
  `sources/manifest.json`. Source PDFs/photos stay in `sources/` (git-ignored, only the manifest is committed).
- Spec-driven models: `projects/<site>/specs/*.yaml`, built with `bm build <site>[/<spec>]`.
- Anything bespoke (films, viewers, bid models): `projects/<site>/products/<name>/` with a `product.yaml`
  listing `steps` (one must be `check`: fast, CPU, no source PDFs; CI runs it). Run with `bm run`.
- Shared code goes in `src/bmodels/`, never imported across sites through `sys.path`. Shared CC0 assets go
  in `assets/`. Repo root in scripts: `from bmodels.paths import ROOT`, not counted `parents[N]`.
- Handover files: `projects/<site>/deliverables/<name>/`.

## Large files

New files over 1 MB go to GitHub Releases: `bm publish <site>/<product> <files…>`, then link the printed
URLs from the deliverable README. Never add new files to Git LFS. `bm check --staged` (pre-commit) and CI
block oversized commits; exceptions go in `.bmcheck.yaml` with a reason.

## Before you finish

- `uv run bm check` (and `bm check-products` if you touched a product) must pass.
- Moving files: `git mv`, keep markdown links relative and valid (`bm check` verifies them), and run
  `bm audit-blends` in CI for any moved `.blend`.
- Commit or push only when asked; branch first if on `main`.

## Working style

Ask once, batched, only for what the documents can't answer (a missing detail, which revision governs).
Otherwise take the next step and mark assumptions. Don't claim accuracy beyond what the sources support.

description: Turn construction drawings, a detail, or site photos into a verified, provenance-tracked Blender model in this repo (new site or new spec). Use when asked to model a building, detail, wall section, room, or repair condition from PDFs or photos.
---

# Model from drawings or photos

Follow `docs/METHOD.md` (rules) and `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (exact commands). This is the order and the gates.

## 0. Orient
```bash
uv run bm doctor          # need: bpy for builds; sources present for intake
uv run bm list --json     # does the site already exist? which specs?
```
If bpy is missing locally, you can still write and validate specs (`bm check`), and CI builds them.

## 1. Site
New jobsite: `uv run bm new <site> --type element|detail --name "<display name>"`, then fill
`projects/<site>/project.yaml` (address, building type, scope). Put source PDFs/photos in
`projects/<site>/sources/` (never committed) and inventory each one in `sources/manifest.json`
(file, sha256, sheet ids, revision/date, scale, photo ids).

## 2. Pick the model type
- **detail**: one section (rake, eave, balcony edge, window head) → start from `templates/project/specs/detail.yaml`;
  example `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-rake-ah700-12.yaml`.
- **house**: plan-extracted shell + takeoff → RUNBOOK steps 2–11; example `projects/qp-cottage-a/specs/qp-cottage-a.yaml`.
- **element**: boxes per member (framing bay, deck) → `templates/project/specs/element.yaml`.
- **room**: photo-only interior → `projects/room-living-kitchen/specs/room-living-kitchen.yaml`.
- Existing condition and proposed repair → two specs (`<x>-existing.yaml`, `<x>-proposed.yaml`).

## 3. Takeoff into the spec (gates)
- Calibrate each sheet from its own dimension strings (`uv run bm calibrate scale …`); never trust the title block.
- Every element: `confirmed` + `source` (dimension on a document), `provisional` + `source` + how measured and
  tolerance, or `assumed` + `basis`. Actual lumber sizes. Never scale an NTS detail.
- Add document-driven `checks` (counts, overall extents, gaps, elevations) each with a `source`.
- Conflicting sources: model the governing one, write the conflict into `flags:`.

## 4. Build and verify
```bash
uv run bm check --no-tests                     # provenance errors without bpy
uv run bm build <site>/<spec> --no-render       # checks only, seconds
uv run bm build <site>/<spec>                   # + review renders in build/<site>/<spec>/
```
Read `build/<site>/<spec>/report.md`, then **look at** the review PNGs (plan/front/side/iso, provenance
colors). Where an elevation exists: `uv run bm overlay …` (RUNBOOK step 10) and report the edge agreement.
No local bpy: push a branch and read the `build-models` run instead.

## 5. Report back
State: checks passed (n/n), renders looked at (which), overlays (agreement %), every assumed element, and
what is not modeled. Never call provisional or assumed geometry documented.
EOF
cat > .claude/skills/ship-deliverable/SKILL.md <<'EOF'
---
name: ship-deliverable
description: Package finished renders, films, .blend/.glb files or viewers as a deliverable in this repo — publish large files to GitHub Releases, write the deliverable README, verify and open a PR. Use when outputs of a product or spec are ready to hand over.
---

# Ship a deliverable

## 1. Where it goes
`projects/<site>/deliverables/<name>/` — the folder listed under `deliverables:` in the product's
`product.yaml` (`uv run bm list --json` shows it). Spec builds land in `build/<site>/<spec>/`; copy what is
handed over from there.

## 2. Large files never go in git
Anything over 1 MB (MP4, .blend, ZIP, EXR, GLB, big GIF/HTML):
```bash
uv run bm publish <site>/<product> <file> [file …]
```
This needs `gh` auth (`bm doctor`) and **creates a public download** on the repo's Releases — confirm with
the user before running it. It records sha256 in the product's `release-assets.json`, adds the files to a
`.gitignore` beside them and prints Markdown links. Commit the manifest and `.gitignore`, not the files.
Keep small previews (PNG/JPG under 1 MB, short GIF) in git so the README renders on GitHub.

## 3. README for the deliverable
Lead with what it is and the preview, then the release links, then:
- sources and their revisions; every assumed or provisional element that is visible;
- "Illustrative, not a contract document" if it can reach a scope, PCO or resident notice;
- how to rebuild: `uv run bm run <site>/<product> <step>` and the product README.
All links relative; `bm check` verifies them.

## 4. Verify and hand off
```bash
uv run bm check                      # links, metadata, large-file guard, tests
uv run bm check-products             # if product code changed
```
Branch, commit, push, `gh pr create`; then read CI (`gh pr checks <n>`). Report what was published
(release tag and links) and what was not verified locally (e.g. bpy or GPU steps that only ran in CI).
EOF
